raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`Glm5NextLinearAttention` cached the merged q|k|v conv weight on the first forward, so an RL refit left the conv kernels reading stale values (#55087). This PR replaces the three `q/k/v_conv1d` modules with a single `conv1d` parameter of shape `[3 * C_local, 1, K]`, which the kernels read directly. Checkpoint `q_conv1d` / `k_conv1d` / `v_conv1d` weights load into it as shards 0/1/2 through `stacked_params_mapping`, using the `_make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader` already used by Kimi-Linear KDA and OLMo-Hybrid GDN. There is no second tensor to keep in sync, so every write path lands in the tensor the kernels read, at a fixed address.

Alternative fixes for the same issue: #56298 and #57638 (see Details; their authors are co-authors on the commit). The fused-parameter design was suggested by hao-aaron in review and replaces this PR's first approach (parameter views into a merged buffer), which broke under weight offloading and `ipc_cache` copy mode.

## Claims

- After `load_weights` / `reload_weights` (checkpoint or kernel format), GLM-5.3 KDA decode uses the refitted conv weights, in eager mode **and** with the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs.
- The conv weight keeps its address across refits, so FULL decode graphs captured before a refit stay valid.
- Works with `--cpu-offload-gb` (with and without refit) and with `--load-format ipc_cache` in both `copy` and `zero_copy` modes.
- No numerical change: the per-rank layout is `[q_r | k_r | v_r]`, the same as the old `torch.cat`. Direct-load outputs are identical to `main`. One copy of the conv weights is dropped.

## Validation

Hardware: GB300 (SM100), TP1, 4-layer pruned GLM-5.3-Flash at full width (`JaredforReal/GLM-5.3-Flash-4L`).

```
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py -v
```

- Unit tests (CPU, `conv1d` sub-module): checkpoint q/k/v shards (2D and 3D) land in q|k|v order; `load_weights`-style refit and a real `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` cycle update the weight without moving it. 22 passed with `test_kda_recurrent.py`.
- `test_refit_reaches_cudagraph_decode[cpu_offload_gb=0|10]` (pruned model, default cudagraphs, one engine per case): direct load -> reference tokens; `reload_weights` of the checkpoint with the conv weights x2 -> output changes; checkpoint as-is -> == reference; kernel-format `reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)` on `conv1d.weight` x2 / x0.5 -> changes / == reference; the conv weight address is identical after all four refits. 2 passed (~5 min each, mostly startup). On `main` the first refit step fails (#55087).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: passed (ruff, mypy, SPDX, test tethering).

CI note: the e2e test is the first in `tests/models/glm5next` to use the pruned checkpoint (19 GB download, needs SM90/SM100, skipped elsewhere). It runs in the existing `glm5next-unit-tests` step; the two offload cases take about 10 min together on GB300, mostly engine startup. #57537 adds a dedicated step for pruned-checkpoint e2e tests that this test could move to once it lands.

Full refit flow, 3 prompts x 24 greedy tokens, compared with `main` direct load:

| tree | config | direct load | dummy -> `reload_weights()` | `load_weights` partial update / kernel-format refit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | cudagraphs | reference | wrong (#55087) | wrong |
| previous revision (buffer views) | cudagraphs | == main | == main | == main |
| previous revision (buffer views) | `cpu_offload_gb=10` | **wrong** | – | – |
| this PR | cudagraphs | == main | == main | == main |
| this PR | eager | == main | == main | == main |
| this PR | `cpu_offload_gb=10` | == main | – | – |

After the reload, every language-model parameter and buffer checksum equals a fresh load.

`--load-format ipc_cache` (a `vllm preload` daemon per GPU, default cudagraphs). After each refit the check compares the conv weight the kernel reads against the checkpoint × scale (max abs diff), then compares the output:

| tree | mode | load | kernel-format refit x2 / x1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | copy | == main | weight stale (diff 0.72), output unchanged (#55087) |
| previous revision (buffer views) | copy | == main | **weight stale (diff 0.72), output unchanged** |
| previous revision (buffer views) | zero_copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main |
| this PR | copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main, address unchanged |
| this PR | zero_copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main, address unchanged |

Checkpoint-format refits are not supported on an `ipc_cache`-loaded model on `main` either, so they're not compared here. `_apply_entries` re-registers every parameter as a plain `nn.Parameter` (399/399 lose `weight_loader`), so `load_weights` of any stacked weight raises `AttributeError` (verified on `main` with `self_attn.q_proj`), and the layerwise `reload_weights` fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor`. On `main` the three conv weights happened to fall through to `default_weight_loader`; with this PR they're stacked like the other projections. Making checkpoint-format refit work after `ipc_cache` is a separate issue.

## Details

**Root cause.** The KDA layer runs one causal conv over the concatenated q|k|v channels. The merged weight was built lazily on the first forward with `torch.cat` and cached, so later writes to `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` (RL refit through the weight-transfer engines, `reload_weights`, or kernel-format `copy_`) never reached it.

**Why not invalidate the cache (#56298, #57638).** Both PRs drop the cached tensor on refit and rebuild it on the next forward. That works with `enforce_eager=True`, but with the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs the KDA forward is captured inside the FULL decode graphs, which keep the old tensor's address, so decode replays never see the rebuilt weight.

**Why one parameter instead of views into a merged buffer.** Views only hold while nothing replaces a parameter's storage. The UVA and prefetch CPU offloaders set each parameter's `.data` right after the layer is built, and the `ipc_cache` loader in copy mode clones every entry separately; either way the three weights stop aliasing the tensor the kernels read. With a single parameter, those paths, the layerwise reload, and kernel-format `copy_` all write the tensor the kernels use. This matches how Kimi-Linear and OLMo-Hybrid already store their fused short convs.

**Trade-offs.**
- The vLLM parameter name changes from `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` to `conv1d.weight`. Checkpoint-format updates keep the HF names and go through the stacked mapping. Kernel-format writers need the fused name, and GLM-5.3 artifacts saved with vLLM parameter names (`sharded_state`, vLLM-serialized tensorizer) before this change will not load.
- Open PRs #59304 (KCP) and #57496 (CPU KDA backend) reference `q_conv1d` / `_merged_conv_weight` and will need a small rebase.

**Not covered here.** The TP2 cudagraph reload drift from the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP8 MoE `gemm1_clamp_limit` tensor and the DSA indexer's lazily cached `_wp_fp32` are separate issues, left for follow-ups.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and the draft of the change; every line was reviewed and the runs above were executed by the submitter.

nodes.body:
Nice find on the FULL-graph address problem. Making the merged weight live at a fixed address is the right goal. I think the aliasing approach can still go stale, though, in two load paths where the q/k/v params stop sharing storage with `_merged_conv_weight`:

1. **Weight offloading** (`--cpu-offload-gb`, UVA or the prefetch offloader).
   - `make_layers` runs the offloader right after each layer's `__init__`. It moves each param's `.data` to new CPU/UVA memory (`offloader/uva.py` `_maybe_offload_to_cpu`, `offloader/prefetch.py:677`). Buffers aren't offloaded.
   - The checkpoint then loads into the offloaded params, while `_merged_conv_weight` keeps its `torch.empty` contents from the first request.
   - On main this case works today, because the lazy `torch.cat` reads the loaded params.
2. **`--load-format ipc_cache` with `mode: copy`.**
   - `_apply_entries` clones each exported tensor separately, so the params and the buffer come back as independent copies.
   - Outputs are correct at startup and go stale after the next refit.

**Suggestion:** fuse the three convs into one param, the way Kimi-Linear's KDA (`kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py`) and OLMo-Hybrid's GDN (`olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py`) already do. Then there's no second tensor to keep in sync:

```python
# kda.py __init__: replaces q/k/v_conv1d, the unsqueezes, and the cached merge
self.conv1d = ColumnParallelLinear(
    input_size=self.conv_size,
    output_size=3 * projection_size,
    bias=False,
    params_dtype=torch.float32,
    prefix=f"{prefix}.conv1d",
)
self.conv1d.weight.data = self.conv1d.weight.data.unsqueeze(1)
delattr(self.conv1d.weight, "weight_loader")
set_weight_attrs(
    self.conv1d.weight,
    {"weight_loader": _make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader(
        [projection_size] * 3, self.tp_size, self.tp_rank)},
)

# _forward
conv_weights = self.conv1d.weight.view(
    self.conv1d.weight.size(0), self.conv1d.weight.size(-1)
)
conv_bias = self.conv1d.bias

# model.py stacked_params_mapping
(".conv1d", ".q_conv1d", 0),
(".conv1d", ".k_conv1d", 1),
(".conv1d", ".v_conv1d", 2),
```

`_make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader` can be imported from `kimi_gdn_linear_attn`, as `kimi_k3/amd/kda.py` already does. It accepts both 2D and 3D checkpoint conv tensors.

From reading the code, this should:
- **keep outputs identical:** the per-rank layout is `[q_r | k_r | v_r]`, the same as today's `torch.cat`;
- **cover every conv call:** the spec-decode, prefill and decode paths already all read the one merged weight;
- **keep a fixed address** for FULL cudagraphs, and make every write path land in the tensor the kernel reads: layerwise reload, kernel-format `copy_`, offloading, and `ipc_cache` copy mode;
- **drop one copy** of the conv weights.

Trade-offs:
- **The param is renamed to `conv1d.weight`.**
  - Kernel-format writers would need the fused name.
  - GLM-5.3 artifacts saved with vLLM param names (`sharded_state`, vLLM-serialized tensorizer) wouldn't load.
  - Checkpoint-format updates keep the HF names and go through the stacked mapping.
- **Tests and other PRs reference the old names:** `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` mocks `q_conv1d` / `_merged_conv_weight`, and #59304 and #57496 reference them too.

Your refit test should carry over, with `conv1d.weight` for the kernel-format step. A `--cpu-offload-gb` run would cover case 1.

Caveat: I haven't tested any of this. It's from reading the code, so please treat it as a suggestion, not a verified fix.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash KDA q|k|v short convs are one fused parameter.
+
+The conv kernels read ``conv1d.weight`` directly, so an RL refit must reach it
+through every write path (#55087), and FULL cudagraphs capture its address, so
+it must never move. Weight offloading replaces parameter storage after
+construction, which the fused parameter must also survive.
+"""
+
+import os
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+from vllm.distributed import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.layerwise import (
+    finalize_layerwise_reload,
+    initialize_layerwise_reload,
+    record_metadata_for_reloading,
+)
+from vllm.models.glm5next.common import kda
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+CHANNELS, KERNEL = 8, 4
+CKPT_CONV_WEIGHTS = ("q_conv1d.weight", "k_conv1d.weight", "v_conv1d.weight")
+# Layers 0-3 of the real checkpoint at full width; needs SM90/SM100 (indexer).
+PRUNED_MODEL = os.getenv("GLM5_PRUNED_MODEL", "JaredforReal/GLM-5.3-Flash-4L")
+
+
+def _checkpoint_weights(seed: int) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    return [torch.randn(CHANNELS, 1, KERNEL, generator=gen) for _ in range(3)]
+
+
+def _load(conv1d: nn.Module, weights: list[torch.Tensor]) -> None:
+    for shard_id, weight in enumerate(weights):
+        conv1d.weight.weight_loader(conv1d.weight, weight, shard_id)
+
+
+def _kernel_view(conv1d: nn.Module) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return conv1d.weight.view(conv1d.weight.size(0), conv1d.weight.size(-1))
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def conv1d(dist_init) -> nn.Module:
+    return kda._fused_qkv_conv1d(KERNEL, CHANNELS, 1, 0, prefix="conv1d")
+
+
+def test_fused_conv_loads_checkpoint_shards_in_qkv_order(conv1d):
+    weights = _checkpoint_weights(seed=0)
+    _load(conv1d, [w.view(CHANNELS, KERNEL) for w in weights[:1]] + weights[1:])
+    assert conv1d.weight.shape == (3 * CHANNELS, 1, KERNEL)
+    assert torch.equal(_kernel_view(conv1d), torch.cat(weights).squeeze(1))
+
+
+def test_refit_updates_fused_conv_without_moving_it(conv1d):
+    """Refits through load_weights (RL weight sync) and through the layerwise
+    reload (``reload_weights``) both land at the original address."""
+    data_ptr = conv1d.weight.data_ptr()
+    _load(conv1d, _checkpoint_weights(seed=0))
+
+    refit = _checkpoint_weights(seed=1)
+    _load(conv1d, refit)
+    assert torch.equal(_kernel_view(conv1d), torch.cat(refit).squeeze(1))
+
+    reload = _checkpoint_weights(seed=2)
+    model = nn.Sequential(conv1d)
+    record_metadata_for_reloading(model)
+    initialize_layerwise_reload(model)
+    _load(conv1d, reload)
+    finalize_layerwise_reload(model, model_config=None)
+    assert torch.equal(_kernel_view(conv1d), torch.cat(reload).squeeze(1))
+    assert conv1d.weight.data_ptr() == data_ptr
+
+
+def _conv_weight_ptrs(model: nn.Module) -> list[int]:
+    return [
+        module.conv1d.weight.data_ptr()
+        for module in model.modules()
+        if isinstance(module, kda.Glm5NextLinearAttention)
+    ]
+
+
+def _refit_from_checkpoint(worker, conv_scale: float) -> list[int]:
+    """RL refit shape: stream the checkpoint through ``reload_weights`` (the
+    layerwise reload), with the KDA conv weights scaled."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import get_model_loader
+
+    runner = worker.model_runner
+    model = runner.get_model()
+    loader = get_model_loader(runner.load_config)
+
+    def weights():
+        for name, tensor in loader.get_all_weights(runner.model_config, model):
+            if name.endswith(CKPT_CONV_WEIGHTS):
+                tensor = tensor * conv_scale
+            yield name, tensor
+
+    worker.reload_weights(weights_iterator=weights())
+    return _conv_weight_ptrs(model)
+
+
+def _refit_kernel_format(worker, conv_scale: float) -> list[int]:
+    """Kernel-format refit: ``reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)``
+    copies into the parameters without any weight loader."""
+    model = worker.model_runner.get_model()
+    weights = [

inline_comments.body: This alias is lost when the model is constructed through the supported `ipc_cache` loader in `mode="copy"`. `_apply_entries` replaces each q/k/v parameter and this buffer independently, and copy mode clones every cache entry (`ipc_loader.py:303-329`), so the parameters no longer share storage with the tensor used by the conv kernel; later refits therefore make this weight stale again. Please re-establish storage-view aliases after IPC entries are applied (or teach the cache protocol to preserve storage views) and cover the copy-mode construction/refit path.

issue_comments.body:
Nice find on the FULL-graph address problem. Making the merged weight live at a fixed address is the right goal. I think the aliasing approach can still go stale, though, in two load paths where the q/k/v params stop sharing storage with `_merged_conv_weight`:

1. **Weight offloading** (`--cpu-offload-gb`, UVA or the prefetch offloader).
   - `make_layers` runs the offloader right after each layer's `__init__`. It moves each param's `.data` to new CPU/UVA memory (`offloader/uva.py` `_maybe_offload_to_cpu`, `offloader/prefetch.py:677`). Buffers aren't offloaded.
   - The checkpoint then loads into the offloaded params, while `_merged_conv_weight` keeps its `torch.empty` contents from the first request.
   - On main this case works today, because the lazy `torch.cat` reads the loaded params.
2. **`--load-format ipc_cache` with `mode: copy`.**
   - `_apply_entries` clones each exported tensor separately, so the params and the buffer come back as independent copies.
   - Outputs are correct at startup and go stale after the next refit.

**Suggestion:** fuse the three convs into one param, the way Kimi-Linear's KDA (`kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py`) and OLMo-Hybrid's GDN (`olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py`) already do. Then there's no second tensor to keep in sync:

```python
# kda.py __init__: replaces q/k/v_conv1d, the unsqueezes, and the cached merge
self.conv1d = ColumnParallelLinear(
    input_size=self.conv_size,
    output_size=3 * projection_size,
    bias=False,
    params_dtype=torch.float32,
    prefix=f"{prefix}.conv1d",
)
self.conv1d.weight.data = self.conv1d.weight.data.unsqueeze(1)
delattr(self.conv1d.weight, "weight_loader")
set_weight_attrs(
    self.conv1d.weight,
    {"weight_loader": _make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader(
        [projection_size] * 3, self.tp_size, self.tp_rank)},
)

# _forward
conv_weights = self.conv1d.weight.view(
    self.conv1d.weight.size(0), self.conv1d.weight.size(-1)
)
conv_bias = self.conv1d.bias

# model.py stacked_params_mapping
(".conv1d", ".q_conv1d", 0),
(".conv1d", ".k_conv1d", 1),
(".conv1d", ".v_conv1d", 2),
```

`_make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader` can be imported from `kimi_gdn_linear_attn`, as `kimi_k3/amd/kda.py` already does. It accepts both 2D and 3D checkpoint conv tensors.

From reading the code, this should:
- **keep outputs identical:** the per-rank layout is `[q_r | k_r | v_r]`, the same as today's `torch.cat`;
- **cover every conv call:** the spec-decode, prefill and decode paths already all read the one merged weight;
- **keep a fixed address** for FULL cudagraphs, and make every write path land in the tensor the kernel reads: layerwise reload, kernel-format `copy_`, offloading, and `ipc_cache` copy mode;
- **drop one copy** of the conv weights.

Trade-offs:
- **The param is renamed to `conv1d.weight`.**
  - Kernel-format writers would need the fused name.
  - GLM-5.3 artifacts saved with vLLM param names (`sharded_state`, vLLM-serialized tensorizer) wouldn't load.
  - Checkpoint-format updates keep the HF names and go through the stacked mapping.
- **Tests and other PRs reference the old names:** `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` mocks `q_conv1d` / `_merged_conv_weight`, and #59304 and #57496 reference them too.

Your refit test should carry over, with `conv1d.weight` for the kernel-format step. A `--cpu-offload-gb` run would cover case 1.

Caveat: I haven't tested any of this. It's from reading the code, so please treat it as a suggestion, not a verified fix.
